findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 6bcbb31c3e2ffd22de4503f2a64cf4d6216382a855b17167ef6cac788bdfe066; all 7 declared sources passed current HTTPS access review.

Claims remain bounded to current official GLO and RRC source roles, form examples, record locators, reporting limits, and no-legal-force or no-private-authority boundaries. Private lease language remains controlling and is not supplied by a public example.

The article publishes no owner document, signature, address, payment instruction, private amount, account detail, well-status finding, lease-effect conclusion, production forecast, valuation input, value, offer, or transaction claim.

sources_inspected.label: Texas General Land Office, Lease Maintenance (accessed 2026-08-23)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official GLO page identifies state-lease maintenance record categories including shut-in payments and affidavits.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only as a bounded public-administration example and expressly rejects importing state-lease requirements or outcomes into a private lease.

sources_inspected.label: Texas General Land Office, Leasing (accessed 2026-08-23)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official GLO leasing page supplies the state-leasing context and official form route.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that route only to identify the source and public-example boundary; it does not substitute GLO materials for an owner controlling document stack.

sources_inspected.label: Texas General Land Office, Relinquishment Act Lease Form (accessed 2026-08-23)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official GLO lease form demonstrates that trigger, covered subject, payment, timing, accompanying-record, duration, and cross-reference wording can occupy separate provisions.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the form only to justify worksheet fields and labels it a state-lease example that supplies no private lease term, deadline, amount, filing duty, or legal result.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Research Queries (accessed 2026-08-23)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official RRC directory links production, permit, well-record, and other regulatory systems and states that online data is informational and lacks legal force.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article requires the exact query, field, identifier, access date, and limitation to remain in a regulatory-context row rather than a private-contract conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Production Data (accessed 2026-08-23)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official RRC production page routes users to compilations and summaries of production information reported by operators.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only to identify the regulatory source class and does not infer a shut-in cause, private clause trigger, production treatment, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Production Data Query System FAQs (accessed 2026-08-23)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official PDQ FAQs explain reporting level, reporting lag, revisions, and snapshot limitations.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those limits to prevent a blank, zero, late, or changed row from becoming proof of a private contract condition or valuation effect.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Well Records (accessed 2026-08-23)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official well-records page identifies useful file-locator fields and states that the Commission lacks authority over private lease, royalty, and property-right matters.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses a well record only as separately labeled regulatory context and does not establish a property connection, status, lease effect, entitlement, or value.
